steps.prompt: Which sentence tells you exactly when it happened?
steps.why: The Present Perfect is about experience, not about when.
steps.html:
He gave his first concert in Tokyo when he was twelve.

He has given concerts all over the world.

steps.title: Present Perfect
steps.html:
FormExample
Positivehave / has + past participleHe has won many prizes.
Negativehaven't / hasn't + participleHe hasn't seen the written music.
QuestionHave / Has + person + participleHave you ever left the cinema early?
Short answerYes, I have. / No, I haven't.
everin questionsHave you ever been to Rio?
never= not everI've never been here before.

Use it to say that something happened in your life, without saying when.

never is already negative: say I've never been, not I haven't never been.

Learners often use the past form after have. It has to be the participle: have seen, not have saw.

Lesson 32 compares this with the Past Simple.

steps.title: Past participles
steps.html:
VerbPast SimpleParticiple
bewas / werebeen
gowentgone / been
seesawseen
dodiddone
writewrotewritten
givegavegiven
winwonwon
havehadhad

Many participles are the same as the Past Simple: won, had, left, met, bought.

For experience we say been: I've been to Rio means you went and came back.
